229	    def get_computed_blocks(self, request: Request) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int]:
230	        """Get the computed (cached) blocks for the request.
231	        Note that the computed blocks must be full.
232	
233	        Args:
234	            request: The request to get the computed blocks.
235	
236	        Returns:
237	            A tuple containing:
238	                - A list of blocks that are computed for the request.
239	                - The number of computed tokens.
240	                - ``shared_prefix_boundary``: the block-aligned token position of
241	                  a shared prefix that a sparse-retention group (Mamba / sliding
242	                  window) has not cached yet (Marconi-style APC), or 0 if none.
243	                  Pinned so ``VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`` does not drop
244	                  the junction and defeat cross-request reuse.
245	        """
246	        # We skip finding the prefix cache hit when prefix caching is
247	        # disabled or the request is marked as skipping kv cache read
248	        # (which happens when the request requires prompt logprobs
249	        # or calls a pooling model with all pooling).
250	        if not self.prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(request):
251	            return self.empty_kv_cache_blocks, 0, 0
252	
253	        # NOTE: When all tokens hit the cache, we must recompute the last token
254	        # to obtain logits. Thus, set max_cache_hit_length to prompt_length - 1.
255	        # This can trigger recomputation of an entire block, rather than just
256	        # the single last token, because allocate_slots() requires
257	        # num_computed_tokens to be block-size aligned. Removing this limitation
258	        # could slightly improve performance in the future.
259	        max_cache_hit_length = request.num_tokens - 1
260	        computed_blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, num_uncached = (
261	            self.coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit(
262	                request.block_hashes, max_cache_hit_length
263	            )
264	        )
265	
266	        # When kv_cache_report_mode is "full", emit BlockStored events
267	        # for the reused prefix cache blocks so that external consumers
268	        # (e.g. gateway) can learn about them.
269	        if (
270	            num_new_computed_tokens > 0
271	            and self.enable_kv_cache_events
272	            and getattr(request, "kv_cache_report_mode", "incremental") == "full"
273	        ):
274	            for group_idx, group_blocks in enumerate(computed_blocks):
275	                num_blocks = len(group_blocks)
276	                if num_blocks > 0:
277	                    group = self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group_idx]
278	                    block_size = group.kv_cache_spec.block_size
279	                    self.block_pool.emit_cached_block_events(
280	                        request,
281	                        num_blocks,
282	                        block_size,
283	                        group_idx,
284	                    )
285	
286	        # The junction to pin is where the lagging sparse-retention group stops
287	        # (``num_new_computed_tokens``) plus the uncached shared prefix -- i.e.
288	        # the longest single-group hit. Sub-block gaps are left to the mask,
289	        # which floors to the alignment boundary (a no-op there).
290	        shared_prefix_boundary = (
291	            num_new_computed_tokens + num_uncached if num_uncached else 0
292	        )
293	
294	        blocks = self.create_kv_cache_blocks(computed_blocks)
295	        return blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, shared_prefix_boundary
296	
297	    def get_computed_blocks_for_connector(
298	        self, request: Request
299	    ) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int, bool]:
300	        """Local prefix-cache lookup for a request scheduled with a KV connector.
301	
302	        Hybrid (Mamba + full-attention) models can have per-group prefix hits
303	        diverge under block pressure: the full-attention tail may be evicted
304	        while a deeper Mamba state survives, or vice versa. Report the
305	        full-attention hit as the local prefix - the connector transfers the
306	        remaining suffix and the Mamba state is transferred unconditionally by
307	        nixl's ``_apply_prefix_caching`` - and flag when that hit ran deeper
308	        than a lagging group. Such a hit only has a valid Mamba state at its
309	        boundary if the connector supplies it, so the caller must fall back to
310	        ``get_computed_blocks`` to reconcile when no external tokens are found.
311	
312	        Non-hybrid models and already-convergent hits use ``get_computed_blocks``.
313	
314	        Returns:
315	            The ``get_computed_blocks`` triple (blocks, number of local computed
316	            tokens, shared-prefix boundary) plus ``hit_diverged``.
317	        """
318	        coordinator = self.coordinator
319	        if not (
320	            self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers
321	            and isinstance(coordinator, HybridKVCacheCoordinator)
322	            and coordinator.full_attention_group_id is not None
323	        ):
324	            return *self.get_computed_blocks(request), False
325	
326	        if not self.prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(request):
327	            return self.empty_kv_cache_blocks, 0, 0, False
328	
329	        fa_group_id = coordinator.full_attention_group_id
330	        computed, per_group_hits = coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit_per_group(
331	            request.block_hashes, request.num_tokens - 1
332	        )
333	        if any(hit > per_group_hits[fa_group_id] for hit in per_group_hits):
334	            # A lagging group hit deeper than full attention means its
335	            # full-attention blocks were evicted; use the reconciled boundary
336	            # that every group agrees on.
337	            return *self.get_computed_blocks(request), False
338	
339	        num_local = per_group_hits[fa_group_id]
340	        blocks = self.create_kv_cache_blocks(computed)
341	        # Per-group lookups do not detect an uncached shared prefix (boundary 0).
342	        return blocks, num_local, 0, min(per_group_hits) < num_local
343	
344	    def allocate_slots(
345	        self,
346	        request: Request,
347	        num_new_tokens: int,
348	        num_new_computed_tokens: int = 0,
349	        new_computed_blocks: KVCacheBlocks | None = None,
350	        num_lookahead_tokens: int = 0,
351	        num_external_computed_tokens: int = 0,
352	        delay_cache_blocks: bool = False,
353	        num_encoder_tokens: int = 0,
354	        full_sequence_must_fit: bool = False,
355	        reserved_blocks: int = 0,
356	        has_scheduled_reqs: bool = True,
357	    ) -> KVCacheBlocks | None:
358	        """Add slots for a request with new tokens to append.
359	
360	        Args:
361	            request: The request to allocate slots.
362	            num_new_tokens: The number of new tokens to be allocated and computed.
363	            num_new_computed_tokens: The number of new computed tokens just
364	                hitting the prefix caching, excluding external tokens.
365	            new_computed_blocks: The cached blocks for the above new computed
366	                tokens, grouped as a tuple by kv cache groups.
367	            num_lookahead_tokens: The number of speculative tokens to allocate.
368	                This is used by spec decode proposers with kv-cache such
369	                as eagle.
370	            num_external_computed_tokens: The number of tokens that their
371	                KV caches are not cached by vLLM but cached by the connector.
372	            delay_cache_blocks: Whether to skip caching the blocks. This is
373	                used by P/D when allocating blocks used in a KV transfer
374	                which will complete in a future step.
375	            num_encoder_tokens: The number of encoder tokens to allocate for
376	                cross-attention in encoder-decoder models(e.g., Whisper).
377	                For decoder-only models, this should be 0.
378	            full_sequence_must_fit: Only allocate blocks if the KV cache has enough
379	                free blocks to hold the full sequence, accounting for prefix cache hits
380	                and sliding window. Used as an admission gate to prevent over-admitting
381	                requests when chunked prefill would otherwise only check the first chunk
382	            reserved_blocks: Number of free blocks that must be left available for
383	                other in-flight sequences to complete. The actual allocation is only
384	                made if it fits within (free blocks - reserved_blocks). Used to gate
385	                async KV-connector loads so their initial allocation cannot consume
386	                blocks an already in-flight (prefilling) sequence is relying on.
387	            has_scheduled_reqs: Whether any requests are already scheduled to run
388	                this step, controls whether watermark is applied.
389	
390	        Blocks layout:
391	        ```
392	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
393	        | < comp > | < new_comp > | < ext_comp >  | < new >  | < lookahead > |
394	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
395	                                                  |   < to be computed >     |
396	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
397	                                  |            < to be allocated >           |
398	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
399	                                  | < to be cached (roughly, |
400	                                  | details below)>          |
401	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
402	        | Prefix-cached tokens from either vLLM   |
403	        | or connector. Can be safely removed if  |
404	        | they are outside sliding window.        |
405	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
406	        |   < cached by vLLM >    | not cached by |
407	                                  | vLLM, but     |
408	        | ref_cnt  | ref_cnt not  | cached by     |
409	        | increased| increased yet| connector     |
410	        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
411	        ```
412	
413	        Abbrivations:
414	
415	        ```
416	        comp      = request.num_computed_tokens
417	        new_comp  = num_new_computed_tokens
418	                  = len(new_computed_blocks) * block_size
419	        ext_comp  = num_external_computed_tokens, cached by the connector
420	        new       = num_new_tokens, including unverified draft tokens
421	        lookahead = num_lookahead_tokens
422	        ```
423	
424	        NOTE: for new tokens which include both verified and unverified draft
425	        tokens, we only cache the verified tokens (by capping the number at
426	        `request.num_tokens`).
427	
428	        The allocation has three stages:
429	        - Free unnecessary blocks in `comp` and check
430	           if we have sufficient free blocks (return None if not).
431	        - Handle prefix tokens (`comp + new_comp + ext_comp`):
432	            - Free unnecessary blocks (e.g. outside sliding window)
433	            - Allocate new blocks for `ext_comp` tokens inside
434	              sliding window
435	        - Allocate new blocks for tokens to be computed (`new + lookahead`)
436	
437	        Returns:
438	            A list of new allocated blocks.
439	        """
440	        # When loading KV data asynchronously, we may have zero new tokens to
441	        # compute while still allocating slots for externally computed tokens.
442	        if num_new_tokens == 0 and num_external_computed_tokens == 0:
443	            raise ValueError(
444	                "num_new_tokens must be greater than 0 when there are no "
445	                "external computed tokens"
446	            )
447	
448	        if new_computed_blocks is not None:
449	            new_computed_block_list = new_computed_blocks.blocks
450	        else:
451	            new_computed_block_list = self.empty_kv_cache_blocks.blocks
452	
453	        # The number of computed tokens is the number of computed tokens plus
454	        # the new prefix caching hits
455	        num_local_computed_tokens = (
456	            request.num_computed_tokens + num_new_computed_tokens
457	        )
458	        total_computed_tokens = min(
459	            num_local_computed_tokens + num_external_computed_tokens,
460	            self.max_model_len,
461	        )
462	
463	        watermark_blocks = 0
464	        # The watermark is applied to waiting/preempted requests only, and only
465	        # when there's at least one request already scheduled.
466	        if has_scheduled_reqs and request.status in (
467	            RequestStatus.WAITING,
468	            RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
469	        ):
470	            watermark_blocks = self.watermark_blocks
471	
472	        if full_sequence_must_fit:
473	            # First check and fail if the full request sequence won't fit.
474	            full_num_tokens = min(request.num_tokens, self.max_model_len)
475	
476	            num_blocks_to_allocate = self.coordinator.get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
477	                request_id=request.request_id,
478	                num_tokens=full_num_tokens,
479	                new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
480	                num_encoder_tokens=num_encoder_tokens,
481	                total_computed_tokens=total_computed_tokens,
482	                num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
483	                num_tokens_main_model=full_num_tokens,
484	                apply_admission_cap=True,
485	            )
486	            required_blocks = num_blocks_to_allocate + watermark_blocks
487	            if required_blocks > self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks():
488	                return None
489	
490	        num_tokens_main_model = total_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens
491	        num_tokens_need_slot = min(
492	            num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, self.max_model_len
493	        )
494	
495	        # Free the blocks that are skipped during the attention computation
496	        # (e.g., tokens outside the sliding window).
497	        # We can do this even if we cannot schedule this request due to
498	        # insufficient free blocks.
499	        # Should call this function before allocating new blocks to reduce
500	        # the number of evicted blocks.
501	        # Free on the processed-token basis: in-flight steps' attention windows
502	        # still read blocks below the optimistic boundary, and rejected spec
503	        # tokens can roll it back.
504	        self.coordinator.remove_skipped_blocks(
505	            request.request_id,
506	            max(0, total_computed_tokens - request.num_in_flight_tokens),
507	            num_prompt_tokens=request.num_prompt_tokens,
508	        )
509	
510	        num_blocks_to_allocate = self.coordinator.get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
511	            request_id=request.request_id,
512	            num_tokens=num_tokens_need_slot,
513	            new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
514	            num_encoder_tokens=num_encoder_tokens,
515	            total_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens
516	            + num_external_computed_tokens,
517	            num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
518	            num_tokens_main_model=num_tokens_main_model,
519	        )
520	
521	        # Keep `reserved_blocks` free for other in-flight sequences, and an
522	        # additional watermark of headroom for waiting/preempted admissions.
523	        available_blocks = self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() - reserved_blocks
524	        required_blocks = num_blocks_to_allocate + watermark_blocks
525	        if required_blocks > available_blocks:
526	            # Cannot allocate new blocks
527	            return None
528	
529	        if (
530	            new_computed_block_list is not self.empty_kv_cache_blocks.blocks
531	            or num_external_computed_tokens > 0
532	        ):
533	            # Append the new computed blocks to the request blocks until now to
534	            # avoid the case where the new blocks cannot be allocated.
535	            self.coordinator.allocate_new_computed_blocks(
536	                request_id=request.request_id,
537	                new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
538	                num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
539	                num_external_computed_tokens=num_external_computed_tokens,
540	            )
541	
542	        new_blocks = self.coordinator.allocate_new_blocks(
543	            request.request_id,
544	            num_tokens_need_slot,
545	            num_tokens_main_model,
546	            num_encoder_tokens,
547	        )
548	
549	        # P/D: delay caching blocks if we have to recv from
550	        # remote. Update state for locally cached blocks.
551	        if not self.enable_caching or delay_cache_blocks:
552	            return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(new_blocks)
553	
554	        # NOTE(woosuk): We want to commit (cache) up to num_local_computed_tokens
555	        # + num_external_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens, but must exclude
556	        # "non-committable" tokens (e.g., draft tokens that could be rejected).
557	        # Therefore, we cap the number at `request.num_tokens`, ensuring only
558	        # "finalized" tokens are cached.
559	        num_tokens_to_cache = min(
560	            total_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens,
561	            request.num_tokens,
562	        )
563	        self.coordinator.cache_blocks(request, num_tokens_to_cache)
564	
565	        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(new_blocks)

567	    def free(self, request: Request) -> None:
568	        """Free the blocks allocated for the request.
569	        We free the blocks in reverse order so that the tail blocks are evicted
570	        first when caching is enabled.
571	
572	        Args:
573	            request: The request to free the blocks.
574	        """
575	        pins = self._partial_tail_pins.pop(request.request_id, None)
576	        if pins:
577	            self.block_pool.free_blocks(pins)
578	        self.coordinator.free(request.request_id)

580	    def remove_skipped_blocks(
581	        self,
582	        request_id: str,
583	        processed_computed_tokens: int,
584	        num_prompt_tokens: int | None = None,
585	    ) -> None:
586	        """Remove the blocks that are no longer needed from `blocks` and replace
587	        the removed blocks with null_block.
588	
589	        Args:
590	            request_id: The request ID.
591	            processed_computed_tokens: Computed-token prefix length covering
592	                fully processed and committed tokens only (safe to free).
593	            num_prompt_tokens: Optional prompt length for R-SWA gap eviction.
594	        """
595	        self.coordinator.remove_skipped_blocks(
596	            request_id, processed_computed_tokens, num_prompt_tokens
597	        )
598	
599	    def pop_blocks_for_free(self, request: Request) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
600	        """Pop the request's bookkeeping and return its blocks without
601	        returning them to the block pool. The caller must eventually free
602	        them in reverse order (so that tail blocks are evicted first).
603	
604	        Args:
605	            request: The request to pop the blocks for.
606	
607	        Returns:
608	            The request's blocks in allocation order.
609	        """
610	        blocks = self.coordinator.pop_blocks_for_free(request.request_id)
611	        # Pins ride the same (possibly deferred) free as the request blocks.
612	        # Preemption may release a pin under a still-queued offload — the same
613	        # exposure normal saves of table blocks already have.
614	        pins = self._partial_tail_pins.pop(request.request_id, None)
615	        if pins:
616	            blocks = pins + blocks
617	        return blocks
618	
619	    def evict_blocks(self, block_ids: set[int]) -> None:
620	        """evict blocks from the prefix cache by their block IDs.
621	
622	        Args:
623	            block_ids: Set of block IDs to evict from cache.
624	        """
625	        self.block_pool.evict_blocks(block_ids)
626	
627	    def reset_prefix_cache(self) -> bool:
628	        """Reset prefix cache. This function may be used in RLHF
629	        flows to invalidate prefix caching after the weights are updated,
630	        or used for resetting prefix caching status for benchmarking.
631	
632	        Returns:
633	            bool: True if the prefix cache is successfully reset,
634	            False otherwise.
635	        """
636	        if not self.block_pool.reset_prefix_cache():
637	            return False
638	        if self.log_stats:
639	            assert self.prefix_cache_stats is not None
640	            self.prefix_cache_stats.reset = True
641	        return True
642	
643	    def get_num_common_prefix_blocks(self, running_request_id: str) -> list[int]:
644	        """Calculate the number of common prefix blocks for each kv cache group.
645	
646	        The function selects a running request and iterates through its blocks.
647	        A block is considered a common prefix block if ALL requests with
648	        allocated KV cache share it (i.e., ref_cnt equals the number of entries
649	        in req_to_blocks).
650	
651	        NOTE(woosuk): The number of requests with allocated KV cache is **greater
652	        than or equal to** the number of requests scheduled in the current step.
653	        This is because having allocated KV cache only indicates that:
654	        1. The request has not yet finished, and
655	        2. The request holds its blocks unfreed.
656	
657	        While all scheduled requests must have allocated KV cache, the inverse
658	        is not necessarily true. There may be requests with allocated KV cache
659	        that are not scheduled in the current step.
660	
661	        This can result in an edge case where the number of common prefix blocks
662	        is 0, even though all scheduled requests share a common prefix. This
663	        occurs because there may be unscheduled requests that do not share the
664	        common prefix. Currently, this case cannot be easily detected, so the
665	        function returns 0 in such cases.
666	
667	        Args:
668	            running_request_id: The request ID of any running request, used to
669	                identify the common prefix blocks.
670	
671	        Returns:
672	            list[int]: The number of common prefix blocks for each kv cache
673	            group.
674	        """
675	        return self.coordinator.get_num_common_prefix_blocks(running_request_id)
676	
677	    def take_events(self) -> list[KVCacheEvent]:
678	        """Take the KV cache events from the block pool.
679	
680	        Returns:
681	            A list of KV cache events.
682	        """
683	        events = self.block_pool.take_events()
684	        for event in events:
685	            if not isinstance(event, BlockStored):
686	                continue
687	            if event.group_idx is None:
688	                continue
689	            if event.group_idx < 0 or event.group_idx >= len(
690	                self.kv_cache_event_metadata
691	            ):
692	                logger.warning(
693	                    "Group index `%s` not in KV cache metadata", event.group_idx
694	                )
695	                continue
696	            # Annotate here so BlockPool can keep emitting structural cache
697	            # events without owning semantic KV cache spec metadata.
698	            kind, sliding_window = self.kv_cache_event_metadata[event.group_idx]
699	            event.kv_cache_spec_kind = kind
700	            event.kv_cache_spec_sliding_window = sliding_window
701	        return events
702	
703	    def get_blocks(self, request_id: str) -> KVCacheBlocks:
704	        """Get the blocks of a request."""
705	        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(self.coordinator.get_blocks(request_id))
706	
707	    def get_block_ids(self, request_id: str) -> tuple[list[int], ...]:
708	        """Get the block ids of a request."""
709	        return self.get_blocks(request_id).get_block_ids()
710	
711	    def get_block_ids_for_computed_tokens(
712	        self,
713	        request_id: str,
714	        num_computed_tokens: int,
715	    ) -> tuple[list[int], ...]:
716	        """Get block ids covering the request's computed tokens."""
717	        block_ids = self.get_block_ids(request_id)
718	        clipped_block_ids: list[list[int]] = []
719	        for group, ids in zip(self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups, block_ids):
720	            spec = group.kv_cache_spec
721	            if not isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec) or isinstance(
722	                spec, (CrossAttentionSpec, EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec)
723	            ):
724	                clipped_block_ids.append(ids)
725	                continue
726	
727	            num_valid_blocks = cdiv(num_computed_tokens, spec.block_size)
728	            clipped_block_ids.append(ids[:num_valid_blocks])
729	        return tuple(clipped_block_ids)
730	
731	    def estimate_cached_tokens(self, request: Request) -> int:
732	        """Estimate the number of tokens cached by the request."""
733	        cached_tokens: int | None = None
734	        for group, blocks in zip(
735	            self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups,
736	            self.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks,
737	        ):
738	            if isinstance(
739	                group.kv_cache_spec,
740	                (CrossAttentionSpec, EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec),
741	            ):
742	                # Cross-attention and encoder-only groups are not prefix cached.
743	                continue
744	
745	            group_cached_tokens = 0
746	            for block in blocks:
747	                group_cached_tokens = max(
748	                    group_cached_tokens,
749	                    block.block_hash_num_tokens or 0,
750	                )
751	
752	            cached_tokens = (
753	                group_cached_tokens
754	                if cached_tokens is None
755	                else min(cached_tokens, group_cached_tokens)
756	            )
757	
758	        return cached_tokens or 0
759	
760	    def cache_blocks(self, request: Request, num_computed_tokens: int) -> None:
761	        """Cache the blocks for the request, if enabled.
762	
763	        Args:
764	            request: The request to cache the blocks.
765	            num_computed_tokens: The number of computed tokens, including tokens
766	                that are already cached and tokens to be cached.
767	        """
768	        if self.enable_caching:
769	            self.coordinator.cache_blocks(request, num_computed_tokens)
770	
771	    def create_kv_cache_blocks(
772	        self, blocks: tuple[list[KVCacheBlock], ...]
773	    ) -> KVCacheBlocks:
774	        # Only create new KVCacheBlocks for non-empty blocks
775	        return KVCacheBlocks(blocks) if any(blocks) else self.empty_kv_cache_blocks
776	
777	    def truncate_computed_blocks(
778	        self, blocks: KVCacheBlocks, num_computed_tokens: int
779	    ) -> KVCacheBlocks:
780	        """Return a lookup-result view truncated at an aligned token endpoint.
781	
782	        Pure slicing: refcounts are untouched and ``blocks`` is not mutated.
783	        """
784	        truncated: list[list[KVCacheBlock]] = []
785	        for group_blocks, manager in zip(
786	            blocks.blocks,
787	            self.coordinator.single_type_managers,
788	            strict=True,
789	        ):
790	            assert num_computed_tokens % manager.block_size == 0
791	            num_blocks = num_computed_tokens // manager.block_size
792	            assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
793	            truncated.append(list(group_blocks[:num_blocks]))
794	        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(tuple(truncated))
795	
796	    def take_new_block_ids(self) -> list[int]:
797	        """Drain and return new attention block IDs for zeroing."""
798	        ids: list[int] = []
799	        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
800	            ids.extend(mgr.take_new_block_ids())
801	        return ids
802	
803	    def get_zeroing_block_ids_in_range(
804	        self, request_id: str, start_token: int, end_token: int
805	    ) -> list[int]:
806	        """The request's block ids covering [start_token, end_token), from
807	        the groups whose new blocks are zeroed by the worker."""
808	        ids: list[int] = []
809	        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
810	            if mgr.records_new_block_ids:
811	                start_idx = start_token // mgr.block_size
812	                end_idx = cdiv(end_token, mgr.block_size)
813	                blocks = mgr.req_to_blocks[request_id]
814	                ids.extend(blk.block_id for blk in blocks[start_idx:end_idx])
815	        return ids
816	
817	    def record_blocks_for_zeroing(self, request_id: str, start_token: int) -> None:
818	        """Re-record the request's blocks from start_token onwards for
819	        zeroing, e.g. blocks a failed async KV load left unwritten.
820	
821	        start_token must be block-aligned: zeroing a partially-valid block
822	        would wipe its valid prefix.
823	        """
824	        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
825	            if mgr.records_new_block_ids:
826	                assert start_token % mgr.block_size == 0
827	                start_idx = start_token // mgr.block_size
828	                blocks = mgr.req_to_blocks[request_id]
829	                mgr.new_block_ids.extend(blk.block_id for blk in blocks[start_idx:])
830	
831	    def take_kv_cache_block_copies(
832	        self,
833	    ) -> tuple[list[KVCacheBlockCopy], list[KVCacheBlock]]:
834	        """Drain pending copies and return their retained endpoints."""
835	        pending_copies: list[tuple[KVCacheBlock, KVCacheBlock]] = []
836	        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
837	            pending_copies.extend(mgr.take_pending_cow_copies())
838	        copies = [
839	            KVCacheBlockCopy(
840	                src_block_id=source_block.block_id,
841	                dst_block_id=cow_block.block_id,
842	            )
843	            for source_block, cow_block in pending_copies
844	        ]
845	        retained_blocks = [block for pair in pending_copies for block in pair]
846	        return copies, retained_blocks
847	
848	    def take_partial_tail_offloads(self) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]]:
849	        """Drain producer partial-tail offload hand-offs per request.
850	
851	        Returns ``{request_id: [(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens), ...]}``
852	        for the durable boundary blocks of producers' last-prompt-boundary
853	        partial tails. Only mamba "align" groups contribute; empty otherwise.
854	        A KV connector reads the referenced blocks and offloads them so a later
855	        request can hit the sub-block prefix.
856	
857	        Each handed-off block lives off the request block table, so it is
858	        pinned here and unpinned when the request's blocks are freed — for a
859	        producer with saved tokens, after the connector reports sends done.
860	        """
861	        offloads: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
862	        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
863	            for (
864	                req_id,
865	                group_id,
866	                block,
867	                boundary_tokens,
868	            ) in mgr.take_pending_partial_tail_offloads():
869	                self.block_pool.touch((block,))
870	                self._partial_tail_pins.setdefault(req_id, []).append(block)
871	                offloads.setdefault(req_id, []).append(
872	                    (group_id, block.block_id, boundary_tokens)
873	                )
874	        return offloads
875	
876	    def new_step_starts(self) -> None:
877	        """Notify the coordinator that a new step is starting."""
878	        self.coordinator.new_step_starts()

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

import itertools
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal, overload

from vllm.distributed.kv_events import BlockStored, KVCacheEvent
from vllm.logger import init_logger
from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_coordinator import (
    HybridKVCacheCoordinator,
    get_kv_cache_coordinator,
)
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_metrics import KVCacheMetricsCollector
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import KVCacheBlock, KVCacheBlockCopy
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
    AttentionSpec,
    CrossAttentionSpec,
    EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec,
    KVCacheConfig,
    get_kv_cache_spec_kind,
    get_kv_cache_spec_sliding_window,
)
from vllm.v1.metrics.stats import PrefixCacheStats
from vllm.v1.request import Request, RequestStatus

logger = init_logger(__name__)


@dataclass
class KVCacheBlocks:
    """
    The allocation result of KVCacheManager, work as the interface between
    Scheduler and KVCacheManager, to hide KVCacheManager's internal data
    structure from the Scheduler.
    """

    blocks: tuple[Sequence[KVCacheBlock], ...]
    """
    `blocks[i][j]` refers to the i-th kv_cache_group
    and the j-th block of tokens.We don't use block of
    tokens as the outer dimension because it assumes all
    kv_cache_groups have the same number of blocks, which is true for now but
    will be broken if we want to give different block_size to different
    kv_cache_groups in the future.

    Each single type KVCacheBlocks could be represented as:
    - list[KVCacheBlock] for more than one KVCacheBlock
    - an empty tuple for requests without KVCacheBlock
      (a precomputed KVCacheBlocks is in KVCacheManager to avoid GC overhead)
    """

    def __add__(self, other: "KVCacheBlocks") -> "KVCacheBlocks":
        """Adds two KVCacheBlocks instances."""
        return KVCacheBlocks(
            tuple(
                list(itertools.chain(blk1, blk2))
                for blk1, blk2 in zip(self.blocks, other.blocks)
            )
        )

    @overload
    def get_block_ids(
        self,
        allow_none: Literal[False] = False,
    ) -> tuple[list[int], ...]: ...

    @overload
    def get_block_ids(
        self,
        allow_none: Literal[True] = True,
    ) -> tuple[list[int], ...] | None: ...

    def get_block_ids(
        self,
        allow_none: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[list[int], ...] | None:
        """
        Converts the KVCacheBlocks instance to block_ids.

        Returns:
            tuple[list[int], ...]: A tuple of lists where:
                - the outer tuple corresponds to KV cache groups
                - each inner list contains the block_ids of the blocks in that
                  group
        """
        if allow_none and all(len(group) == 0 for group in self.blocks):
            return None
        return tuple([blk.block_id for blk in group] for group in self.blocks)

    def get_unhashed_block_ids(self) -> list[int]:
        """Get block_ids of unhashed blocks from KVCacheBlocks instance."""
        assert len(self.blocks) == 1, "Only one group is supported"
        return [block.block_id for block in self.blocks[0] if block.block_hash is None]

    def get_unhashed_block_ids_all_groups(self) -> list[list[int]]:
        """Get block_ids of unhashed blocks from KVCacheBlocks instance."""
        # Skip padding blocks.
        return [
            [
                block.block_id
                for block in group
                if block.block_hash is None and not block.is_null
            ]
            for group in self.blocks
        ]

    def new_empty(self) -> "KVCacheBlocks":
        """
        Creates a new KVCacheBlocks instance with no blocks.
        """
        return KVCacheBlocks(tuple(() for _ in range(len(self.blocks))))


class KVCacheManager:
    def __init__(
        self,
        kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
        max_model_len: int,
        scheduler_block_size: int,
        hash_block_size: int,
        max_in_flight_tokens: int | None = None,
        enable_caching: bool = True,
        use_eagle: bool = False,
        log_stats: bool = False,
        enable_kv_cache_events: bool = False,
        dcp_world_size: int = 1,
        pcp_world_size: int = 1,
        metrics_collector: KVCacheMetricsCollector | None = None,
        watermark: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.max_model_len = max_model_len
        # When unset, fall back to `max_model_len` so the recycling-aware cap
        # collapses to the prior (uncapped) admission behavior. The scheduler
        # always supplies the real value at runtime.
        if max_in_flight_tokens is None:
            max_in_flight_tokens = max_model_len

        self.enable_caching = enable_caching
        self.enable_kv_cache_events = enable_kv_cache_events
        self.use_eagle = use_eagle
        self.log_stats = log_stats
        self.metrics_collector = metrics_collector
        # FIXME: make prefix cache stats conditional on log_stats. We still need
        # this comment because when the log stats is enabled there are still
        # potential configs we could expose in the future.
        self.prefix_cache_stats = PrefixCacheStats() if log_stats else None

        self.coordinator = get_kv_cache_coordinator(
            kv_cache_config=kv_cache_config,
            max_model_len=self.max_model_len,
            max_in_flight_tokens=max_in_flight_tokens,
            use_eagle=self.use_eagle,
            enable_caching=self.enable_caching,
            enable_kv_cache_events=enable_kv_cache_events,
            dcp_world_size=dcp_world_size,
            pcp_world_size=pcp_world_size,
            scheduler_block_size=scheduler_block_size,
            hash_block_size=hash_block_size,
            metrics_collector=self.metrics_collector,
        )
        self.num_kv_cache_groups = len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)
        self.block_pool = self.coordinator.block_pool
        self.kv_cache_config = kv_cache_config

        # Watermark: minimum number of KV cache blocks to keep free when
        # admitting waiting/preempted requests, to avoid frequent preemptions.
        assert watermark >= 0.0, "watermark must be non-negative"
        self.watermark_blocks = int(watermark * kv_cache_config.num_blocks)
        self.kv_cache_event_metadata = tuple(
            (
                get_kv_cache_spec_kind(group.kv_cache_spec).value,
                get_kv_cache_spec_sliding_window(group.kv_cache_spec),
            )
            for group in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups
        )

        # Pre-constructed KVCacheBlocks with no blocks, callers should use this
        # via create_kv_cache_blocks instead of creating new ones to avoid GC
        # overhead.
        #
        # We use nested tuples to ensure the empty KVCacheBlocks is immutable.
        self.empty_kv_cache_blocks = KVCacheBlocks(
            tuple(() for _ in range(self.num_kv_cache_groups))
        )

        # Off-table cow blocks handed to a KV connector for partial-tail
        # offload; pinned until the request's blocks are freed.
        self._partial_tail_pins: dict[str, list[KVCacheBlock]] = {}

    @property
    def usage(self) -> float:
        """Get the KV cache usage.

        Returns:
            The KV cache usage (between 0.0 and 1.0).
        """
        return self.block_pool.get_usage()

    def make_prefix_cache_stats(self) -> PrefixCacheStats | None:
        """Get (and reset) the prefix cache stats.

        Returns:
            The current prefix caching stats, or None if logging is disabled.
        """
        if not self.log_stats:
            return None
        stats = self.prefix_cache_stats
        self.prefix_cache_stats = PrefixCacheStats()
        return stats

    def prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(self, request: Request) -> bool:
        """Whether a local prefix cache lookup may be run for this request."""
        return self.enable_caching and not request.skip_reading_prefix_cache

    def record_prefix_cache_stats(self, request: Request, num_hits: int) -> None:
        # Don't count a request that skipped the cache lookup.
        if not self.log_stats or not self.prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(request):
            return
        assert self.prefix_cache_stats is not None
        self.prefix_cache_stats.record(
            num_tokens=request.num_tokens,
            num_hits=num_hits,
            preempted=request.num_preemptions > 0,
        )

    def get_computed_blocks(self, request: Request) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int]:
        """Get the computed (cached) blocks for the request.
        Note that the computed blocks must be full.

        Args:
            request: The request to get the computed blocks.

        Returns:
            A tuple containing:
                - A list of blocks that are computed for the request.
                - The number of computed tokens.
                - ``shared_prefix_boundary``: the block-aligned token position of
                  a shared prefix that a sparse-retention group (Mamba / sliding
                  window) has not cached yet (Marconi-style APC), or 0 if none.
                  Pinned so ``VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`` does not drop
                  the junction and defeat cross-request reuse.
        """
        # We skip finding the prefix cache hit when prefix caching is
        # disabled or the request is marked as skipping kv cache read
        # (which happens when the request requires prompt logprobs
        # or calls a pooling model with all pooling).
        if not self.prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(request):
            return self.empty_kv_cache_blocks, 0, 0

        # NOTE: When all tokens hit the cache, we must recompute the last token
        # to obtain logits. Thus, set max_cache_hit_length to prompt_length - 1.
        # This can trigger recomputation of an entire block, rather than just
        # the single last token, because allocate_slots() requires
        # num_computed_tokens to be block-size aligned. Removing this limitation
        # could slightly improve performance in the future.
        max_cache_hit_length = request.num_tokens - 1
        computed_blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, num_uncached = (
            self.coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit(
                request.block_hashes, max_cache_hit_length
            )
        )

        # When kv_cache_report_mode is "full", emit BlockStored events
        # for the reused prefix cache blocks so that external consumers
        # (e.g. gateway) can learn about them.
        if (
            num_new_computed_tokens > 0
            and self.enable_kv_cache_events
            and getattr(request, "kv_cache_report_mode", "incremental") == "full"
        ):
            for group_idx, group_blocks in enumerate(computed_blocks):
                num_blocks = len(group_blocks)
                if num_blocks > 0:
                    group = self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group_idx]
                    block_size = group.kv_cache_spec.block_size
                    self.block_pool.emit_cached_block_events(
                        request,
                        num_blocks,
                        block_size,
                        group_idx,
                    )

        # The junction to pin is where the lagging sparse-retention group stops
        # (``num_new_computed_tokens``) plus the uncached shared prefix -- i.e.
        # the longest single-group hit. Sub-block gaps are left to the mask,
        # which floors to the alignment boundary (a no-op there).
        shared_prefix_boundary = (
            num_new_computed_tokens + num_uncached if num_uncached else 0
        )

        blocks = self.create_kv_cache_blocks(computed_blocks)
        return blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, shared_prefix_boundary

    def get_computed_blocks_for_connector(
        self, request: Request
    ) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int, bool]:
        """Local prefix-cache lookup for a request scheduled with a KV connector.

        Hybrid (Mamba + full-attention) models can have per-group prefix hits
        diverge under block pressure: the full-attention tail may be evicted
        while a deeper Mamba state survives, or vice versa. Report the
        full-attention hit as the local prefix - the connector transfers the
        remaining suffix and the Mamba state is transferred unconditionally by
        nixl's ``_apply_prefix_caching`` - and flag when that hit ran deeper
        than a lagging group. Such a hit only has a valid Mamba state at its
        boundary if the connector supplies it, so the caller must fall back to
        ``get_computed_blocks`` to reconcile when no external tokens are found.

        Non-hybrid models and already-convergent hits use ``get_computed_blocks``.

        Returns:
            The ``get_computed_blocks`` triple (blocks, number of local computed
            tokens, shared-prefix boundary) plus ``hit_diverged``.
        """
        coordinator = self.coordinator
        if not (
            self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers
            and isinstance(coordinator, HybridKVCacheCoordinator)
            and coordinator.full_attention_group_id is not None
        ):
            return *self.get_computed_blocks(request), False

        if not self.prefix_cache_lookup_enabled(request):
            return self.empty_kv_cache_blocks, 0, 0, False

        fa_group_id = coordinator.full_attention_group_id
        computed, per_group_hits = coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit_per_group(
            request.block_hashes, request.num_tokens - 1
        )
        if any(hit > per_group_hits[fa_group_id] for hit in per_group_hits):
            # A lagging group hit deeper than full attention means its
            # full-attention blocks were evicted; use the reconciled boundary
            # that every group agrees on.
            return *self.get_computed_blocks(request), False

        num_local = per_group_hits[fa_group_id]
        blocks = self.create_kv_cache_blocks(computed)
        # Per-group lookups do not detect an uncached shared prefix (boundary 0).
        return blocks, num_local, 0, min(per_group_hits) < num_local

    def allocate_slots(
        self,
        request: Request,
        num_new_tokens: int,
        num_new_computed_tokens: int = 0,
        new_computed_blocks: KVCacheBlocks | None = None,
        num_lookahead_tokens: int = 0,
        num_external_computed_tokens: int = 0,
        delay_cache_blocks: bool = False,
        num_encoder_tokens: int = 0,
        full_sequence_must_fit: bool = False,
        reserved_blocks: int = 0,
        has_scheduled_reqs: bool = True,
    ) -> KVCacheBlocks | None:
        """Add slots for a request with new tokens to append.

        Args:
            request: The request to allocate slots.
            num_new_tokens: The number of new tokens to be allocated and computed.
            num_new_computed_tokens: The number of new computed tokens just
                hitting the prefix caching, excluding external tokens.
            new_computed_blocks: The cached blocks for the above new computed
                tokens, grouped as a tuple by kv cache groups.
            num_lookahead_tokens: The number of speculative tokens to allocate.
                This is used by spec decode proposers with kv-cache such
                as eagle.
            num_external_computed_tokens: The number of tokens that their
                KV caches are not cached by vLLM but cached by the connector.
            delay_cache_blocks: Whether to skip caching the blocks. This is
                used by P/D when allocating blocks used in a KV transfer
                which will complete in a future step.
            num_encoder_tokens: The number of encoder tokens to allocate for
                cross-attention in encoder-decoder models(e.g., Whisper).
                For decoder-only models, this should be 0.
            full_sequence_must_fit: Only allocate blocks if the KV cache has enough
                free blocks to hold the full sequence, accounting for prefix cache hits
                and sliding window. Used as an admission gate to prevent over-admitting
                requests when chunked prefill would otherwise only check the first chunk
            reserved_blocks: Number of free blocks that must be left available for
                other in-flight sequences to complete. The actual allocation is only
                made if it fits within (free blocks - reserved_blocks). Used to gate
                async KV-connector loads so their initial allocation cannot consume
                blocks an already in-flight (prefilling) sequence is relying on.
            has_scheduled_reqs: Whether any requests are already scheduled to run
                this step, controls whether watermark is applied.

        Blocks layout:
        ```
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
        | < comp > | < new_comp > | < ext_comp >  | < new >  | < lookahead > |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                  |   < to be computed >     |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
                                  |            < to be allocated >           |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
                                  | < to be cached (roughly, |
                                  | details below)>          |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
        | Prefix-cached tokens from either vLLM   |
        | or connector. Can be safely removed if  |
        | they are outside sliding window.        |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
        |   < cached by vLLM >    | not cached by |
                                  | vLLM, but     |
        | ref_cnt  | ref_cnt not  | cached by     |
        | increased| increased yet| connector     |
        ----------------------------------------------------------------------
        ```

        Abbrivations:

        ```
        comp      = request.num_computed_tokens
        new_comp  = num_new_computed_tokens
                  = len(new_computed_blocks) * block_size
        ext_comp  = num_external_computed_tokens, cached by the connector
        new       = num_new_tokens, including unverified draft tokens
        lookahead = num_lookahead_tokens
        ```

        NOTE: for new tokens which include both verified and unverified draft
        tokens, we only cache the verified tokens (by capping the number at
        `request.num_tokens`).

        The allocation has three stages:
        - Free unnecessary blocks in `comp` and check
           if we have sufficient free blocks (return None if not).
        - Handle prefix tokens (`comp + new_comp + ext_comp`):
            - Free unnecessary blocks (e.g. outside sliding window)
            - Allocate new blocks for `ext_comp` tokens inside
              sliding window
        - Allocate new blocks for tokens to be computed (`new + lookahead`)

        Returns:
            A list of new allocated blocks.
        """
        # When loading KV data asynchronously, we may have zero new tokens to
        # compute while still allocating slots for externally computed tokens.
        if num_new_tokens == 0 and num_external_computed_tokens == 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "num_new_tokens must be greater than 0 when there are no "
                "external computed tokens"
            )

        if new_computed_blocks is not None:
            new_computed_block_list = new_computed_blocks.blocks
        else:
            new_computed_block_list = self.empty_kv_cache_blocks.blocks

        # The number of computed tokens is the number of computed tokens plus
        # the new prefix caching hits
        num_local_computed_tokens = (
            request.num_computed_tokens + num_new_computed_tokens
        )
        total_computed_tokens = min(
            num_local_computed_tokens + num_external_computed_tokens,
            self.max_model_len,
        )

        watermark_blocks = 0
        # The watermark is applied to waiting/preempted requests only, and only
        # when there's at least one request already scheduled.
        if has_scheduled_reqs and request.status in (
            RequestStatus.WAITING,
            RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
        ):
            watermark_blocks = self.watermark_blocks

        if full_sequence_must_fit:
            # First check and fail if the full request sequence won't fit.
            full_num_tokens = min(request.num_tokens, self.max_model_len)

            num_blocks_to_allocate = self.coordinator.get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
                request_id=request.request_id,
                num_tokens=full_num_tokens,
                new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
                num_encoder_tokens=num_encoder_tokens,
                total_computed_tokens=total_computed_tokens,
                num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
                num_tokens_main_model=full_num_tokens,
                apply_admission_cap=True,
            )
            required_blocks = num_blocks_to_allocate + watermark_blocks
            if required_blocks > self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks():
                return None

        num_tokens_main_model = total_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens
        num_tokens_need_slot = min(
            num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, self.max_model_len
        )

        # Free the blocks that are skipped during the attention computation
        # (e.g., tokens outside the sliding window).
        # We can do this even if we cannot schedule this request due to
        # insufficient free blocks.
        # Should call this function before allocating new blocks to reduce
        # the number of evicted blocks.
        # Free on the processed-token basis: in-flight steps' attention windows
        # still read blocks below the optimistic boundary, and rejected spec
        # tokens can roll it back.
        self.coordinator.remove_skipped_blocks(
            request.request_id,
            max(0, total_computed_tokens - request.num_in_flight_tokens),
            num_prompt_tokens=request.num_prompt_tokens,
        )

        num_blocks_to_allocate = self.coordinator.get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
            request_id=request.request_id,
            num_tokens=num_tokens_need_slot,
            new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
            num_encoder_tokens=num_encoder_tokens,
            total_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens
            + num_external_computed_tokens,
            num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
            num_tokens_main_model=num_tokens_main_model,
        )

        # Keep `reserved_blocks` free for other in-flight sequences, and an
        # additional watermark of headroom for waiting/preempted admissions.
        available_blocks = self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() - reserved_blocks
        required_blocks = num_blocks_to_allocate + watermark_blocks
        if required_blocks > available_blocks:
            # Cannot allocate new blocks
            return None

        if (
            new_computed_block_list is not self.empty_kv_cache_blocks.blocks
            or num_external_computed_tokens > 0
        ):
            # Append the new computed blocks to the request blocks until now to
            # avoid the case where the new blocks cannot be allocated.
            self.coordinator.allocate_new_computed_blocks(
                request_id=request.request_id,
                new_computed_blocks=new_computed_block_list,
                num_local_computed_tokens=num_local_computed_tokens,
                num_external_computed_tokens=num_external_computed_tokens,
            )

        new_blocks = self.coordinator.allocate_new_blocks(
            request.request_id,
            num_tokens_need_slot,
            num_tokens_main_model,
            num_encoder_tokens,
        )

        # P/D: delay caching blocks if we have to recv from
        # remote. Update state for locally cached blocks.
        if not self.enable_caching or delay_cache_blocks:
            return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(new_blocks)

        # NOTE(woosuk): We want to commit (cache) up to num_local_computed_tokens
        # + num_external_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens, but must exclude
        # "non-committable" tokens (e.g., draft tokens that could be rejected).
        # Therefore, we cap the number at `request.num_tokens`, ensuring only
        # "finalized" tokens are cached.
        num_tokens_to_cache = min(
            total_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens,
            request.num_tokens,
        )
        self.coordinator.cache_blocks(request, num_tokens_to_cache)

        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(new_blocks)

    def free(self, request: Request) -> None:
        """Free the blocks allocated for the request.
        We free the blocks in reverse order so that the tail blocks are evicted
        first when caching is enabled.

        Args:
            request: The request to free the blocks.
        """
        pins = self._partial_tail_pins.pop(request.request_id, None)
        if pins:
            self.block_pool.free_blocks(pins)
        self.coordinator.free(request.request_id)

    def remove_skipped_blocks(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        processed_computed_tokens: int,
        num_prompt_tokens: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Remove the blocks that are no longer needed from `blocks` and replace
        the removed blocks with null_block.

        Args:
            request_id: The request ID.
            processed_computed_tokens: Computed-token prefix length covering
                fully processed and committed tokens only (safe to free).
            num_prompt_tokens: Optional prompt length for R-SWA gap eviction.
        """
        self.coordinator.remove_skipped_blocks(
            request_id, processed_computed_tokens, num_prompt_tokens
        )

    def pop_blocks_for_free(self, request: Request) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
        """Pop the request's bookkeeping and return its blocks without
        returning them to the block pool. The caller must eventually free
        them in reverse order (so that tail blocks are evicted first).

        Args:
            request: The request to pop the blocks for.

        Returns:
            The request's blocks in allocation order.
        """
        blocks = self.coordinator.pop_blocks_for_free(request.request_id)
        # Pins ride the same (possibly deferred) free as the request blocks.
        # Preemption may release a pin under a still-queued offload — the same
        # exposure normal saves of table blocks already have.
        pins = self._partial_tail_pins.pop(request.request_id, None)
        if pins:
            blocks = pins + blocks
        return blocks

    def evict_blocks(self, block_ids: set[int]) -> None:
        """evict blocks from the prefix cache by their block IDs.

        Args:
            block_ids: Set of block IDs to evict from cache.
        """
        self.block_pool.evict_blocks(block_ids)

    def reset_prefix_cache(self) -> bool:
        """Reset prefix cache. This function may be used in RLHF
        flows to invalidate prefix caching after the weights are updated,
        or used for resetting prefix caching status for benchmarking.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the prefix cache is successfully reset,
            False otherwise.
        """
        if not self.block_pool.reset_prefix_cache():
            return False
        if self.log_stats:
            assert self.prefix_cache_stats is not None
            self.prefix_cache_stats.reset = True
        return True

    def get_num_common_prefix_blocks(self, running_request_id: str) -> list[int]:
        """Calculate the number of common prefix blocks for each kv cache group.

        The function selects a running request and iterates through its blocks.
        A block is considered a common prefix block if ALL requests with
        allocated KV cache share it (i.e., ref_cnt equals the number of entries
        in req_to_blocks).

        NOTE(woosuk): The number of requests with allocated KV cache is **greater
        than or equal to** the number of requests scheduled in the current step.
        This is because having allocated KV cache only indicates that:
        1. The request has not yet finished, and
        2. The request holds its blocks unfreed.

        While all scheduled requests must have allocated KV cache, the inverse
        is not necessarily true. There may be requests with allocated KV cache
        that are not scheduled in the current step.

        This can result in an edge case where the number of common prefix blocks
        is 0, even though all scheduled requests share a common prefix. This
        occurs because there may be unscheduled requests that do not share the
        common prefix. Currently, this case cannot be easily detected, so the
        function returns 0 in such cases.

        Args:
            running_request_id: The request ID of any running request, used to
                identify the common prefix blocks.

        Returns:
            list[int]: The number of common prefix blocks for each kv cache
            group.
        """
        return self.coordinator.get_num_common_prefix_blocks(running_request_id)

    def take_events(self) -> list[KVCacheEvent]:
        """Take the KV cache events from the block pool.

        Returns:
            A list of KV cache events.
        """
        events = self.block_pool.take_events()
        for event in events:
            if not isinstance(event, BlockStored):
                continue
            if event.group_idx is None:
                continue
            if event.group_idx < 0 or event.group_idx >= len(
                self.kv_cache_event_metadata
            ):
                logger.warning(
                    "Group index `%s` not in KV cache metadata", event.group_idx
                )
                continue
            # Annotate here so BlockPool can keep emitting structural cache
            # events without owning semantic KV cache spec metadata.
            kind, sliding_window = self.kv_cache_event_metadata[event.group_idx]
            event.kv_cache_spec_kind = kind
            event.kv_cache_spec_sliding_window = sliding_window
        return events

    def get_blocks(self, request_id: str) -> KVCacheBlocks:
        """Get the blocks of a request."""
        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(self.coordinator.get_blocks(request_id))

    def get_block_ids(self, request_id: str) -> tuple[list[int], ...]:
        """Get the block ids of a request."""
        return self.get_blocks(request_id).get_block_ids()

    def get_block_ids_for_computed_tokens(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        num_computed_tokens: int,
    ) -> tuple[list[int], ...]:
        """Get block ids covering the request's computed tokens."""
        block_ids = self.get_block_ids(request_id)
        clipped_block_ids: list[list[int]] = []
        for group, ids in zip(self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups, block_ids):
            spec = group.kv_cache_spec
            if not isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec) or isinstance(
                spec, (CrossAttentionSpec, EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec)
            ):
                clipped_block_ids.append(ids)
                continue

            num_valid_blocks = cdiv(num_computed_tokens, spec.block_size)
            clipped_block_ids.append(ids[:num_valid_blocks])
        return tuple(clipped_block_ids)

    def estimate_cached_tokens(self, request: Request) -> int:
        """Estimate the number of tokens cached by the request."""
        cached_tokens: int | None = None
        for group, blocks in zip(
            self.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups,
            self.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks,
        ):
            if isinstance(
                group.kv_cache_spec,
                (CrossAttentionSpec, EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec),
            ):
                # Cross-attention and encoder-only groups are not prefix cached.
                continue

            group_cached_tokens = 0
            for block in blocks:
                group_cached_tokens = max(
                    group_cached_tokens,
                    block.block_hash_num_tokens or 0,
                )

            cached_tokens = (
                group_cached_tokens
                if cached_tokens is None
                else min(cached_tokens, group_cached_tokens)
            )

        return cached_tokens or 0

    def cache_blocks(self, request: Request, num_computed_tokens: int) -> None:
        """Cache the blocks for the request, if enabled.

        Args:
            request: The request to cache the blocks.
            num_computed_tokens: The number of computed tokens, including tokens
                that are already cached and tokens to be cached.
        """
        if self.enable_caching:
            self.coordinator.cache_blocks(request, num_computed_tokens)

    def create_kv_cache_blocks(
        self, blocks: tuple[list[KVCacheBlock], ...]
    ) -> KVCacheBlocks:
        # Only create new KVCacheBlocks for non-empty blocks
        return KVCacheBlocks(blocks) if any(blocks) else self.empty_kv_cache_blocks

    def truncate_computed_blocks(
        self, blocks: KVCacheBlocks, num_computed_tokens: int
    ) -> KVCacheBlocks:
        """Return a lookup-result view truncated at an aligned token endpoint.

        Pure slicing: refcounts are untouched and ``blocks`` is not mutated.
        """
        truncated: list[list[KVCacheBlock]] = []
        for group_blocks, manager in zip(
            blocks.blocks,
            self.coordinator.single_type_managers,
            strict=True,
        ):
            assert num_computed_tokens % manager.block_size == 0
            num_blocks = num_computed_tokens // manager.block_size
            assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
            truncated.append(list(group_blocks[:num_blocks]))
        return self.create_kv_cache_blocks(tuple(truncated))

    def take_new_block_ids(self) -> list[int]:
        """Drain and return new attention block IDs for zeroing."""
        ids: list[int] = []
        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
            ids.extend(mgr.take_new_block_ids())
        return ids

    def get_zeroing_block_ids_in_range(
        self, request_id: str, start_token: int, end_token: int
    ) -> list[int]:
        """The request's block ids covering [start_token, end_token), from
        the groups whose new blocks are zeroed by the worker."""
        ids: list[int] = []
        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
            if mgr.records_new_block_ids:
                start_idx = start_token // mgr.block_size
                end_idx = cdiv(end_token, mgr.block_size)
                blocks = mgr.req_to_blocks[request_id]
                ids.extend(blk.block_id for blk in blocks[start_idx:end_idx])
        return ids

    def record_blocks_for_zeroing(self, request_id: str, start_token: int) -> None:
        """Re-record the request's blocks from start_token onwards for
        zeroing, e.g. blocks a failed async KV load left unwritten.

        start_token must be block-aligned: zeroing a partially-valid block
        would wipe its valid prefix.
        """
        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
            if mgr.records_new_block_ids:
                assert start_token % mgr.block_size == 0
                start_idx = start_token // mgr.block_size
                blocks = mgr.req_to_blocks[request_id]
                mgr.new_block_ids.extend(blk.block_id for blk in blocks[start_idx:])

    def take_kv_cache_block_copies(
        self,
    ) -> tuple[list[KVCacheBlockCopy], list[KVCacheBlock]]:
        """Drain pending copies and return their retained endpoints."""
        pending_copies: list[tuple[KVCacheBlock, KVCacheBlock]] = []
        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
            pending_copies.extend(mgr.take_pending_cow_copies())
        copies = [
            KVCacheBlockCopy(
                src_block_id=source_block.block_id,
                dst_block_id=cow_block.block_id,
            )
            for source_block, cow_block in pending_copies
        ]
        retained_blocks = [block for pair in pending_copies for block in pair]
        return copies, retained_blocks

    def take_partial_tail_offloads(self) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]]:
        """Drain producer partial-tail offload hand-offs per request.

        Returns ``{request_id: [(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens), ...]}``
        for the durable boundary blocks of producers' last-prompt-boundary
        partial tails. Only mamba "align" groups contribute; empty otherwise.
        A KV connector reads the referenced blocks and offloads them so a later
        request can hit the sub-block prefix.

        Each handed-off block lives off the request block table, so it is
        pinned here and unpinned when the request's blocks are freed — for a
        producer with saved tokens, after the connector reports sends done.
        """
        offloads: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
        for mgr in self.coordinator.single_type_managers:
            for (
                req_id,
                group_id,
                block,
                boundary_tokens,
            ) in mgr.take_pending_partial_tail_offloads():
                self.block_pool.touch((block,))
                self._partial_tail_pins.setdefault(req_id, []).append(block)
                offloads.setdefault(req_id, []).append(
                    (group_id, block.block_id, boundary_tokens)
                )
        return offloads

    def new_step_starts(self) -> None:
        """Notify the coordinator that a new step is starting."""
        self.coordinator.new_step_starts()

33	class BlockHashToBlockMap:
34	    """
35	    Cache of blocks that are used for prefix caching. It caches blocks
36	    from hash directly to a block or multiple blocks
37	    (i.e. {block_hash: KVCacheBlocks})
38	    - Mostly block_hash maps to a single KVCacheBlock, and KVCacheBlocks
39	        would simply be a KVCacheBlock.
40	    - Otherwise, KVCacheBlocks is a dict from {block_id: KVCacheBlock}
41	
42	    A cached block is a full block with a block hash that can be used
43	    for prefix caching.
44	    The cached block may be used by running requests or in the
45	    free_block_queue that could potentially be evicted.
46	
47	    NOTE #1: We currently don't de-duplicate the blocks in the cache,
48	    meaning that if a block becomes full and is cached, we don't check
49	    if there is already an identical block in the cache. This is because
50	    we want to make sure the allocated block IDs won't change so that
51	    block tables are append-only.
52	    NOTE #2: The union type is introduced in order to reduce GC costs
53	    from the inner dict.
54	    """
55

57	        self._cache: dict[
58	            BlockHashWithGroupId, KVCacheBlock | dict[int, KVCacheBlock]
59	        ] = {}
60	
61	    def get_one_block(self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId) -> KVCacheBlock | None:
62	        """
63	        Gets any block with the given block hash key.
64	        """
65	        blocks = self._cache.get(key)
66	        if blocks is not None:
67	            if isinstance(blocks, KVCacheBlock):
68	                return blocks
69	            if isinstance(blocks, dict):
70	                return next(iter(blocks.values()))
71	            self._unexpected_blocks_type(blocks)
72	        return None
73	
74	    def contain(self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, block_id: int) -> bool:
75	        """
76	        Checks whether the key maps to the given block ID.
77	        """
78	        blocks = self._cache.get(key)
79	        if blocks is None:
80	            return False
81	        if isinstance(blocks, KVCacheBlock):
82	            return blocks.block_id == block_id
83	        if isinstance(blocks, dict):
84	            return block_id in blocks
85	        self._unexpected_blocks_type(blocks)
86	        return False

88	    def insert(self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, block: KVCacheBlock) -> None:
89	        """
90	        Inserts the KVCacheBlock to the cache
91	        """
92	        blocks = self._cache.get(key)
93	        if blocks is None:
94	            # When key is not found, attach a single block to the key
95	            self._cache[key] = block
96	        elif isinstance(blocks, KVCacheBlock):
97	            # If there's a block with the same key, merge the original block
98	            # and the new block into a dict
99	            self._cache[key] = {blocks.block_id: blocks, block.block_id: block}
100	        elif isinstance(blocks, dict):
101	            # If it's already a dict, simply insert the block
102	            blocks[block.block_id] = block
103	        else:
104	            self._unexpected_blocks_type(blocks)
105	
106	    def pop(self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, block_id: int) -> KVCacheBlock | None:
107	        """
108	        Checks if block_hash exists and pop block_id from the cache
109	        """
110	        blocks = self._cache.pop(key, None)
111	        if blocks is None:
112	            # block_hash not found in the cache
113	            return None
114	        # TODO(Jialin): If key is found, block_id should always present
115	        # in blocks. We currently keep the original behaviour for safety.
116	        #
117	        # Will add block_id == blocks.block_id assertion and
118	        # use del blocks[block_id] instead as followup.
119	        if isinstance(blocks, KVCacheBlock):
120	            if blocks.block_id == block_id:
121	                return blocks
122	            # If the single block ID doesn't match, we should put the
123	            # block back (it should happen rarely)
124	            self._cache[key] = blocks
125	            return None
126	        if isinstance(blocks, dict):
127	            # Try to pop block_id from the block dict, and if dict still
128	            # contain blocks, put back to the cache.
129	            block = blocks.pop(block_id, None)
130	            if len(blocks) > 0:
131	                self._cache[key] = blocks
132	            return block
133	        self._unexpected_blocks_type(blocks)
134	        return None
135	
136	    def __len__(self) -> int:
137	        return len(self._cache)
138	
139	    def _unexpected_blocks_type(self, blocks: Any) -> None:
140	        raise AssertionError(f"Invalid KV cache block type {type(blocks)}")
